title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
abstract: arXiv:2610.20582v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. translated_title: 基于测试时训练的潜在压缩
translated_abstract: 长上下文会扩大键值（KV）缓存，增加生成过程中的内存使用和注意力计算成本。压缩这些缓存时必须为未见过的问 题保留信息。我们提出了**潜在压缩**，该方法通过测试时训练学习一个紧凑的、针对特定文档的缓存。我们使用重构 重要性、教师注意力和键空间多样性来初始化缓存条目。训练首先将注意力输出和对数归一化器拟合到完整缓存的对应 值，其中由重构选出的条目保持固定；随后通过从完整缓存模型进行端到端蒸馏，联合优化整个缓存。整个过程模型权 重保持冻结，训练仅使用关于文档的通用提示，无法访问下游的问题或答案。在 RULER、LongBench 和 Phonebook Lookup 上的实验表明，该方法相较于预算相当的压缩基线取得了显著提升。例如在 RULER 上，我们的方法实现了……（摘要截断）
tldr: 提出“潜在压缩”方法，通过测试时训练在模型权重冻结且不接触下游问题的情况下，学习紧凑的文档级 KV 缓存，显著优于同等预算的缓存压缩基线。
en_tdlr: Latent Compaction learns a compact document-specific KV cache via test-time training with frozen model weights and no access to downstream questions, substantially outperforming budget-matched compression baselines on long-context benchmarks.
